claims.text: A TiZrNbHfTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating will be deposited on TC4 by a CAA spray process.
The CAA spray parameters of 500 °C preheating, 50 mm spray distance, and 30 kW arc power are optimized for this coating system.
The deposited coating will receive a post-deposition heat treatment at 600 °C for 2 hours.
The intervention will form a dense coating.
The intervention will form a compositionally homogeneous coating.
The intervention will form a strongly bonded coating on TC4.
The resulting coating will be 200 μm thick.
The resulting coating will contain a stable oxide layer.
Post-deposition heat treatment promotes formation of the stable oxide layer.
Post-deposition heat treatment relieves residual stresses in the RHEA coating.
Stable-oxide formation and residual-stress relief enhance the coating's mechanical properties.
The intervention will increase hardness relative to untreated TC4, reaching up to 500 HV.
The intervention will improve wear resistance relative to untreated TC4 by 50%.
The intervention will preserve TC4's original advantages.
The predicted performance applies at loads up to 1000 N.
The predicted performance applies at a sliding speed of 0.5 m/s.
The post-deposition heat treatment may cause residual stresses and cracking in the RHEA coating.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improved wear resistance, whereas the parenthetical phrase 'wear resistance (reduced by 50%)' literally indicates that wear resistance itself decreases. This would be coherent only if the intended quantity were wear rate, wear volume, or mass loss.

The structural mediator confidently specifies a strongly bonded coating, while the uncertainty acknowledges possible heat-treatment-induced residual stress and cracking that could undermine bonding and mechanical stability. The risk is not incorporated into a conditional prediction.
